regions.summary: Write three single-sprite shots to OAM, hiding inactive entries with Y=$F0. Outside the boss stage, schedule enemy animation, motion, spawning, explosions and OAM composition in READY or play. Find an inactive slot whose stage timer expired, choose a top hatch from paddle position and initialize species animation/movement pointers using stage modulo four. Hatch state 5 releases the enemy. Initialize the chosen enemy slot only when the hatch sequence reaches its release state. For three active enemies, run emergence, free movement and exit state handlers every third tick. Move out of the hatch, then navigate the brick grid until a clear lower area permits a scripted trajectory. Below the arena switch to vertical exit. Read paired signed displacement commands forward/backward; $80 reverses the script. Mirror horizontal motion at boundaries and enter exit below the arena. Move a departing enemy down until Y reaches $F0, then free the slot. Try one-pixel motion according to five navigation states. Roll back blocked axes, turn at arena/grid limits and use enemy-overlap tests plus state mixing to choose detours. At vertical grid crossings, test up to two overlapped cells. Return carry for a blocking brick or the upper limit. Check left/right limits and up to three vertically overlapped brick cells at horizontal grid crossings. Carry means blocked. When another enemy overlaps below, choose a sideways route or a bounded upward detour using the state mixer. Carry indicates a selected avoidance route. If an overlapping enemy is above this slot, turn downward; return carry only when handled. For overlap on the left, choose a timed upward detour. For overlap on the right, turn left; carry reports handling. Search the other two active slots for intersecting fifteen-pixel bounds. Carry reports overlap and Y identifies the other slot. Compute row*11+column from enemy pixel Y/X relative to $10, then add the active player playfield base into SourcePointer. Advance each active enemy species tile stream on its timer. $FF wraps the stream to its first tile; the first slot uses a longer cadence. Advance defeated enemies through the explosion tile table, with a sound on the first phase; zero terminates and hides the sprite.
